The quiet art of keeping things simple.

Most things in life, work, and cooking do not fail for a lack of effort. They fail because they gather clutter. When you remove what does not matter, clarity, speed, and flavour take care of themselves.

THE THREE DESKS

What You Will
Find Here.

Everything here comes from personal experience: thirty years of loving, cooking, building companies, and surviving. I write to separate what truly matters from everyday noise, in the hope that these notes make your life, your table, and your work a little simpler.

01
FOLIO / 01

Life, Relationships, & Perspective

Life has a quiet way of teaching us through observation, patience, and warmth. I do not write to give romantic advice or pretend to be wise. I write about what growing up in a not-so-big city of Lucknow, learning the nuances of communication and tehzeeb, raising a daughter, and building things from scratch have taught me about becoming a kinder human being. Simple reflections on patience, fatherhood, and keeping your dignity intact.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
•Why everyone should fall in love at least once in their lifetime
•The quiet wisdom of long devotion and arranged partnerships
•Perspective over panic: un-complicating everyday human life
LIFE
EVERY TWO WEEKS
02
PANTRY / 02

Comfort Food, 5 Spices or Less

In Lucknow, where I come from, the nose makes the final judgement before the tongue ever gets a turn. Good food does not need thirty jars of spices. It needs good aroma, deliberate heat, and simple steps. I cook purely for the joy of it, using five spices or fewer. Every fortnight, I share one simple, comforting recipe that anyone can master.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
•One foolproof, tested recipe every fortnight
•Mastering the 5-spice alchemy from Cumin to Aromatics
•How deliberate cooking clears and calms a cluttered executive mind
FOOD
FORTNIGHTLY RECIPE
03
CABINET / 03

Career, Startups & Boardrooms

Thirty years of enterprise building ventures, nurturing teams, and learning what truly endures. From assembling computers in my Lucknow bedroom to navigating boardroom conversations, scaling hardware startups, and managing clean exits, I have seen what works and what is pure theatre. I share a weekly note on career navigation, practical leadership, and cutting through operational noise.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
•How to navigate organisational politics and accelerate career growth
•Building from zero: customer acquisition, hiring, and unit economics
•Investor relations, board dynamics, and the discipline of clean exits

Operational Clarity

The Five Essentials

Five simple rules are enough to run any venture, and few enough that nothing gets lost. When you clear away the noise, what truly matters becomes obvious.

LEVER 0101

The Foundations

“Patience with the base.”

Endurance is built in unglamorous unit economics and cash discipline, long before vanity metrics enter the room.

DISCIPLINE
LEVER 0202

Ground Truth

“Tasting without illusions.”

Unvarnished reality over comforting spreadsheets. In boardrooms and co-founder partnerships, plain truth builds unbreakable trust.

CANDOR
LEVER 0303

Cohesion

“The silent binder.”

Keeping mission, incentives, and execution cadence tightly aligned so teams move with speed and zero political friction.

ALIGNMENT
LEVER 0404

Calculated Risk

“High flame with purpose.”

Playing not to lose guarantees slow attrition. Category leadership demands decisive, asymmetric bets when conviction matures.

CONVICTION
LEVER 0505

Restraint

“Discipline of the stop.”

Knowing when the work is resolved, resisting feature bloat, and having the courage to leave the core value uncrowded.

FOCUS
THE MAN BEHIND THE DESKS · VIVEK SHUKLA
“If falling in love three times was not quite dramatic enough, I decided to almost die once, just to keep things interesting.”

From assembling computers in my college bedroom to surviving a craniotomy at 27, relearning speech from scratch, building India's water sub-metering category across four regional offices, and steering an orderly exit. I write because survival taught me to pay attention, and I advise because I know how lonely the founder's chair can get.
